entities.name: Edwin, son of Edward the Elder
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Edwin, son of Edward the Elder, was a significant figure in the Anglo-Saxon period. He was the younger son of King Edward the Elder and Ælfflæd, his second wife, and drowned at sea in 933 CE. This event had a profound impact on the succession of the English monarchy, as Edward's oldest son Æthelstan was passed over for the throne in favor of Æthelstan's half-brother Æthelflæd's son, Æthelstan's own son Æthelweard being bypassed for the title of King of England, and Æthelstan being declared King of England, following the death of King Edmund Ironside, and later being crowned King of England at the age of 22. This marked the beginning of the House of Wessex, which would go on to dominate English history for centuries.

Edwin was also a key figure in the Mercian succession crisis of 924 CE, as the Mercians chose Æthelstan as their king, while the West Saxons selected Æthelstan's half-brother Æthelweard. This led to a period of instability and conflict in the region, which would continue for decades.

Despite his significance, Edwin's life and legacy are relatively poorly documented, and much of what is known about him comes from brief mentions in historical records.

Edwin's death at sea in 933 CE was a significant event, as it marked the end of an era and the beginning of a new period of English history. His legacy can be seen in the many descendants of Æthelstan, who would go on to shape English history for centuries to come.
